name: PCRF Treatment Abroad Program
description: The Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF) arranges free medical care for sick and injured children from the Middle East and developing countries who cannot receive adequate treatment in their home countries. Since 1992, PCRF has sent over 2,000 children to hospitals in the USA, Europe, and Asia for free care. The program covers surgical procedures, hospitalization, international travel, and aftercare for children with conditions including cardiac defects, orthopedic injuries, burn injuries, and cancer. Volunteer medical teams also travel to the region to provide care directly.
eligibility: Children from the Middle East and developing countries who cannot receive adequate medical care in their home countries; referrals accepted from hospitals and medical professionals
amount: Full treatment costs covered (surgery, travel, hospitalization)
targetDiagnosis: Cardiac defects, orthopedic injuries, burn injuries, cancer, congenital conditions
applicationProcess: Referrals are accepted from hospitals and medical professionals in the Middle East region. Families or doctors submit a medical case file through the PCRF website or local field offices. PCRF's medical advisory board reviews cases and matches children with appropriate hospitals and volunteer surgeons in the US, Europe, or Asia.
geographicScope: International — patients from Palestine, Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, Iraq; treatment in USA, Europe, Asia
documentsRequired: Medical records, diagnosis documentation, referral from treating physician, passport or travel document for child

name: Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program
description: The Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program is the largest federally funded program in the United States for people living with HIV/AIDS. Critically for immigrants, this program does not use immigration status as a factor in determining eligibility. It provides comprehensive medical services, antiretroviral medications, dental care, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, case management, and emergency financial assistance to low-income individuals who are uninsured or underinsured.
eligibility: Individuals living with HIV/AIDS who are uninsured or underinsured and have low income; immigration status is NOT a determining factor for eligibility
amount: Varies by service — covers medications, medical care, and support services
applicationProcess: Contact your local Ryan White-funded clinic or AIDS Service Organization (ASO). Eligibility is determined at the local provider level based on income, HIV status, and insurance status. No immigration documentation required. Find local providers through the HRSA HIV/AIDS Bureau locator.
geographicScope: United States — all 50 states, territories, and the District of Columbia
documentsRequired: Proof of HIV diagnosis, proof of income/financial need, identification (flexible forms accepted)

name: ERDERA Joint Transnational Research Calls — Rare Diseases
description: ERDERA (European Rare Diseases Research Alliance) funds cross-border rare disease research through joint transnational calls, clinical trials calls, and networking support schemes. Part of the EU Horizon Europe framework with over €800 million committed, the program bridges gaps in scientific knowledge, fosters international collaboration, and delivers tangible benefits to patients affected by rare diseases across Europe. Funded projects improve access to specialized treatment centers, develop new therapies, and build patient registries that enable affected individuals to connect with clinical trials regardless of their country of residence.
eligibility: Research consortia involving institutions from at least 3 participating EU/associated countries; patients with rare diseases who may benefit from cross-border access to clinical trials
amount: €100,000 – €500,000 per project; part of €800M+ Horizon Europe commitment
targetDiagnosis: Rare diseases (defined as affecting fewer than 5 in 10,000 people in the EU)
applicationProcess: Calls are published on the ERDERA website and EU Funding & Tenders portal. Research teams form international consortia and submit joint applications during open call periods. Patient advocacy organizations may also apply for networking support. Check erdera.org/funding for current open calls and deadlines.
geographicScope: European Union and associated countries — cross-border collaboration required
documentsRequired: Research proposal, consortium agreement, institutional endorsements, ethical approval, patient engagement plan

name: MRFF 2026 International Clinical Trial Collaborations Grant
organization: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC)
description: The Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) 2026 International Clinical Trial Collaborations Grant supports Australian involvement in international collaborative investigator-initiated clinical trials research. The program enables international patients to gain access to novel treatments through collaborative trials conducted across borders. It aims to increase clinical trial activity, improve the evidence base supporting clinical care, and bring innovative therapies to patients in Australia and partner countries.
eligibility: Australian research institutions collaborating with international partners; international patients may access treatments through participation in funded trials
targetDiagnosis: Various — depends on specific clinical trial focus areas
applicationProcess: Applications submitted through NHMRC's online portal during the open grant round. Research institutions must demonstrate international collaboration with at least one partner institution abroad. Review the grant opportunity guidelines (GO8232) on the NHMRC website for specific requirements and deadlines.
geographicScope: Australia — with mandatory international collaboration component
documentsRequired: Research proposal, clinical trial protocol, ethics approval, international collaboration agreement, budget justification, track record of investigators

name: Hydrocephalus Association — Next Generation Travel Award
description: The Hydrocephalus Association Next Generation Travel Award supports early-career hydrocephalus researchers from around the world to attend the National Conference on Hydrocephalus (HA CONNECT). The award covers travel, accommodation, and conference registration costs. It is specifically designed to help international researchers who would otherwise be unable to attend, fostering global collaboration in hydrocephalus research and advancing treatment options for patients worldwide.
eligibility: Early-career hydrocephalus researchers worldwide, including international researchers; must be actively conducting research related to hydrocephalus
amount: Up to $3,000 per awardee (travel, accommodation, registration)
applicationProcess: Apply through the Hydrocephalus Association website during the open application period (typically several months before the annual conference). Submit CV, research summary, letter of support from mentor/supervisor, and statement explaining how attendance will advance your hydrocephalus research.
geographicScope: International — researchers from any country may apply
documentsRequired: CV/resume, research summary, letter of support from supervisor, personal statement, proof of early-career status

name: DEBRA International EB2026 Travel Grant
description: DEBRA International and DEBRA Research provide travel grants to support patients, clinicians, and researchers working on Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB) who would otherwise not be able to attend the EB2026 international congress. The grants cover travel and accommodation costs, enabling knowledge exchange and access to the latest treatment advances for this rare genetic skin condition. The program specifically targets representatives from low-resource settings and developing countries to ensure equitable global participation in rare disease research.
eligibility: EB patients, clinicians, and researchers who would otherwise be unable to attend the EB2026 congress; priority given to representatives from low-resource settings
applicationProcess: Apply through the DEBRA Research website during the open application window. Submit a brief application explaining your connection to EB research or care, your need for financial support, and how attending EB2026 will benefit your work or patient community.
documentsRequired: Application form, proof of involvement in EB research/care/advocacy, budget estimate for travel
